mutations.because: toBrief must save through the validator's parser: reverting the seed to parseInt truncates a free-typed `1e5` (validated as 100000) back to 1, and emits NaN for a blank draft, which the X18 agreement test catches as a save that is not the validated value.

The validator must accept exactly what the helper saves: `Number("42.0")` is the integer 42, so reverting this gate to Number re-accepts a decimal-form draft that parsePolicyInteger — and therefore toBrief — refuses, and the agreement test fails on a validated value that is never saved.

Every reader of a policy integer must use the one parser: reverting the count readout to Number.parseInt truncates the accepted, saveable draft "1e5" back to 1 on screen, and the PolicySection X18 test — which asserts the readout speaks 100000 (and the slider sits at the ceiling), not parseInt's 1 — fails.

canPlan must refuse a plan whose optional draft toBrief would silently omit: dropping the draftOrParsed conjuncts lets a "12abc" seed or "42.0" perProduct draft plan anyway, and the canPlan X18 test — false for a refused draft, true when blank — fails.

An unsafe integer is not the integer it validates as: reverting to Number.isInteger re-accepts "9007199254740993", which Number reads as the representable 9007199254740992, so the draft validates as one integer while toBrief saves another — the exact invariant this lane exists for — and the X18 unsafe-integer test fails on a parse that must return undefined.
